speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee
text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance in light of the issues with GIRO deductions faced by parents following the closure of a student care chain (a) whether the Minister can clarify what safeguards exist within the GIRO framework to prevent duplicate or erroneous debits; and (b) whether the Ministry will review the framework to strengthen consumer protections, including mandatory pre-debit notifications and consumer set limits on variable deductions.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance in addition to the limits-per-transaction for GIRO deductions and safeguards against scams, whether MAS will consider requiring banks to allow customers to set optional limits on the number or cumulative amount of deductions per billing period for individual GIRO arrangements, so as to improve customer control against bad actors or technical failure in company payment systems.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance whether the Government can provide information on (a) what due diligence checks are banks required to conduct when onboarding a corporate customer for GIRO billing; and (b) whether banks are required to have suspicious transactions alerts when a billing organisation deducts multiple GIRO transactions from a customer in a short time span.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: However, checks by banks may not always be able to prevent errors and potential misuse of GIRO.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We will also consider suggestions by Ms Gho Sze Kee, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Shawn Loh, and members of the public.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We also advise consumers to review their current GIRO arrangements and to set appropriate transaction limits with their banks and financial institutions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: There are also other non-GIRO payment options available to consumers including standing instructions to the bank for recurring monthly payments for an amount set by the customer.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: In the United Kingdom, the Bankers Automated Clearing Services operates widely used direct debit scheme that includes advance notice of payment amounts, a direct debit guarantee, allowing for immediate refunds in case of error and strong consumer recourse mechanisms.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: So, in light of these established safeguards in other countries, could the Minister of State clarify whether Singapore's review of the GIRO framework would move towards incorporating such similar features?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I would say also that now, some of the banks have, for example, GIRO on-demand, where each deduction must be authorised individually before the bank processes the transaction.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, different banks have different ways either to implement safeguards or have different safeguards.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We will look into also setting monthly limits for transaction amounts and also, the value of transactions, and then, also, to enhance monitoring of transactions.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: I am very heartened to hear it, that MAS has agreed to do a review because the current level of consumer protections are not adequate.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: The first one is how long will this review take?

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: And my second question is, while the review is ongoing, can MAS also increase public awareness of the protections offered to consumers, as well as the limitations?

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: So, today, you can only set a limit per transaction, but consumers are not protected because agencies or organisations can have multiple deductions within that transaction limit.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: So, can public awareness be increased prior to the review being completed?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And in the review, we will start with lower-hanging fruits.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But we accept and we will take his views into account.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The Consumer Association of Singapore (CASE) will be happy to work with MAS on consumer protection measures.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: For consumers, we often use GIRO when we want to so call, "set and forget", recurring payments.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: And therefore, we acknowledge that while there is convenience of using GIRO, it also comes with trade-off, including the possibility of fraud.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Many consumers regard GIRO as a secure and convenient means of payment, and therefore, we must put in place the necessary safeguards.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I want to ask whether there are existing thresholds or guidelines for banks to therefore flag anomalous GIRO deduction patterns?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: If not, whether MAS intends to introduce such standards for the banks?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Because when we do GIRO, we forget about it and we expect that the banks protect us by monitoring certain patterns.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As he mentioned earlier on, GIRO has its uses.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For example, if you were to pay your monthly electricity bills, this affords convenience, because the bills will fluctuate from month to month.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But there are also some downsides, and that is why this review will take into account what he, Ms Gho and Mr Shawn Loh have suggested, and that includes also enhance monitoring of transactions as well.
